commits.edited_message:
ar: Add Windows Archive file support

Archives in ar format as written by Windows tools like lib.exe, separate
strings in string table directly with \0 instead of /\n.

GNU ar translates backslashes into slashes before the /\n check.

Handle both for improved compatibility, which also allows ar archives to
contain files in a directory structure.

Windows tables are already NUL-separated, so keep the final pad byte
instead of overwriting it. Long-name offsets are limited to the
terminated part of the copied image.

Resolves #546

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

ar: Do not expose GNU filename table

The filename table is used for long filenames of actual file entries.
Continue reading headers until a real file entry is consumed.

Otherwise ar archives would list "//" as actual content, which GNU ar
does not.

A long-name offset that lands on a string-table separator is not a
name. Resolve it to the tail of the table, which is empty when the
image is terminated.

Resolves #2291

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

ar: Always skip all special entry bytes

The special file entries / and // are supposed to be properly padded,
but don't implicitly rely on it. Use archive_read_format_ar_skip
instead which takes care of possible padding bytes.

An even-sized filename table is padded by two bytes that are not part
of the copied image. Count them in the logical length, and clamp
long-name lookup back to the image.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

coupling: The over-read is in the GNU/Windows ar long-name lookup: archive_entry_copy_pathname() runs strlen on a pointer into the filename-table image. Three changes each stay inside the allocation, and each pair is enough to walk off it. (1) 28b2bcd records the copied length in strtab_alloc and, for a Windows table that is already NUL-separated, keeps the final pad byte instead of forcing a trailing NUL. Offsets into that unterminated pad are rejected, and the lookup only moves a separator offset to the last copied byte when the logical length is later extended past strtab_alloc, which this commit never does. (2) 2e5abe1 resolves an offset that lands on a separator to strtab_size-1. That index is inside the image, and every table this commit still terminates, so the copy stops on the NUL. (3) 7af7f26 adds two to the logical length of an even table (the pad bytes that were not copied) and clamps the lookup limit back by the same amount, so a caller-supplied offset still cannot address the pad. Dropping (3) leaves (1)+(2): separator resolution lands on the non-NUL pad byte kept by (1) and strlen continues past the image. Dropping (2) leaves (1)+(3): the extended length makes (1) move the separator offset onto that same non-NUL byte. Dropping (1) leaves (2)+(3): separator resolution uses the unclamped logical length and reads one past the allocation. Reverting any single edited diff therefore leaves a reachable heap over-read, and no one diff indexes outside the buffer it allocated.
